news.title: Premier League 2 report: Cobham Next Gen 2-2 Liverpool
news.body_en: Chelsea Cobham Next Gen were forced to settle for a point in Premier League 2 this afternoon after a 2-2 draw against Liverpool at Kingsmeadow. Harrison McMahon broke the deadlock inside two minutes with a powerful finish into the bottom corner. Sol Gordon then added to the scoreline midway through the opening period with a first-time strike beyond Harvey Davies to put the Blues in control. Minutes later, though, we were pegged back as Will Wright made it 2-1. Although we went in ahead at the break, Liverpool scored another early in the second half through a Jayden Danns free-kick. Both sides pushed for a late winner, but the spoils were shared. Chelsea set the tone immediately, scoring within two minutes through McMahon. Chizaram Ezenwata picked up the ball centrally and turned before playing a pass into McMahon’s path, and the midfielder made no mistake with his low-driven strike across goal. Ezenwata, who claimed the assist for the opener, caused the Liverpool’s backline constant problems, getting on the ball in deep areas and driving forwards. He wasn’t far away from doubling our lead when he found half a yard on Reds defender Talla Ndiaye, but his effort went just wide. Our speed constantly caused issues for the visitors' defence, with Mathis Eboue and Gordon enjoying plenty of success down the flanks. It was the latter who doubled our advantage, finishing a well-worked move. Ezenwata held the ball up well and forced his marker to bring him down. That enabled Kendry Paez to emerge with the ball and burst forward. Just as Ecuadorian looked like he was going to shoot, he instead chopped inside onto his right foot and selflessly passed to Gordon, who dispatched a fine finish past Davies. Five minutes after Gordon scored, Wright pulled one back for the visitors, capitalising on their only meaningful chance of the half. After the break, Liverpool pulled themselves back level with Danns converting from a free-kick. He placed his strike into the bottom corner, beyond the outstretched glove of Freddy Bernal. Liverpool continued to put us under pressure, with Prince Cisse hitting the post and Oliver O'Connor missing a clear-cut chance. We pushed for a late winner but were ultimately forced to settle for a point. After six games, this draw leaves us on 13 points in Premier League 2 and in second position. The league leaders are ahead via goal difference with a game in hand. Cobham Next Gen are kickstart their UEFA Youth League campaign on Wednesday 28 October, when we face Estonian side Flora Tallinn at the Lillekula Stadium. The game gets underway at 5pm BST and supporters can watch the match live with a CFC+ subscription. news.title: Xabi Alonso on Tottenham defeat: 'We all take the blame'
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso was disappointed with the performance and result against Tottenham Hotspur and accepted his Chelsea side 'can do better' after succumbing to a two-goal defeat at Stamford Bridge. During a rain-soaked 90 minutes in SW6, both sides created goalscoring opportunities across the 90 minutes. Cole Palmer forced Antonin Kinsky into a good first-half save, and Jordan Henderson, Morgan Rogers and Pedro Neto were also denied by the Tottenham goalkeeper. Mike Penders made good stops of his own, first to deny Omar Marmoush and then Mathys Tel. However, with 13 minutes remaining, Tottenham forced a Penders own goal from a corner and, after Palmer was dismissed for two yellow cards, Tel struck late on to seal a rare Spurs' victory at Stamford Bridge. Alonso was honest in his post-match assessment, acknowledging the performance was not at the level the Blues had displayed in our back-to-back wins over Bournemouth and Everton. ‘We all take the blame for the result and for the performance,' he said. 'Today we were not at our best. I felt that in the second half, the game was even and could have gone either way. Once we conceded that first goal, and then with the red card, it was difficult.' The Blues manager continued: 'In the second half, it was tight, with some half-chances for them and half-chances for us. It was about taking a moment and once we conceded the first goal, it conceded everything. Then, when we wanted to have a reaction, we got the red card. Then it went the other way. 'We can do better. It's one to reflect after this big game that it was against a good opponent. And the performance, it's one to improve.' The Blues' preparation for the game was disrupted with Joao Pedro sustaining an injury in training on the eve of Tottenham's visit. And Alonso said the absence of the Brazilian forward did mean a late change to the game plan was needed. He said: 'We had to take many decisions in a short time. What we had been working on in the week, you need to be flexible and adapt. So it changed the idea we had a little bit, but this is football, and it can happen. 'It’s no secret that with Joao we are better, but it’s not about talking about the players missing. It’s about the players who were on the pitch. We can do better and we have to be critical of ourselves.'

news.title: Highlights: Chelsea 0-2 Spurs
Match report: Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham Hotspur
news.body_en: It proved a disappointing evening for the Blues at Stamford Bridge as we were beaten by Tottenham Hotspur. For much of the contest, little separated the two sides. In the opening period, Cole Palmer and Jordan Henderson forced Antonin Kinsky into good saves. Mike Penders, meanwhile, produced good stops to deny Omar Marmoush and Mathys Tel. The second period remained tight, but with 13 minutes to play, a Tottenham corner ended up in the Blues' goal via the hand of Penders, who was put under pressure by Jan Paul van Hecke. Palmer was then shown a red card after receiving two yellows inside ten minutes, and Tel netted late on for Tottenham to condemn the Blues to defeat. Xabi Alonso was forced to make two changes to his starting XI. Emi Martinez and Joao Pedro both missed out due to injuries –the latter sustaining an issue in training yesterday – and were replaced by Penders and Geovany Quenda. The opening 45 minutes were played in a downpour. It meant every touch had to be precise and every pass weighted perfectly. The Blues looked more threatening in the early stages and kept Tottenham at arm's length. Our first chance of note was fashioned as the game approached the quarter-hour mark. Pedro Neto started it as he won the ball near the corner flag and fed it to Morgan Rogers inside the box. The England international laid it first-time to Palmer, who whipped his shot to the far post from an acute angle. However, Antonin Kinsky saved well. As the half progressed, Spurs took a stranglehold of possession. Mohammed Kudus had the visitors' first shot of the evening – an attempt from inside the box that flew wide – before a good chance was created for Omar Marmoush from 10 yards. Penders reacted quickly to produce an excellent stop. The Belgian goalkeeper produced an even better save soon after, rushing out and diving at the feet of Mathys Tel to deny the forward's left-footed strike. Alonso's side responded to the Spurs' attempts. The first came following a mistake from Kinsky, which enabled Neto, Rogers and Palmer to exchange one-touch passes in the Tottenham penalty area and lay the ball to Henderson. The Blues midfielder attempted to guide his finish into the corner, but put it close enough to Kinsky to allow the goalkeeper to save. Rogers was next denied as he drove a left-footed strike at goal, but the offside flag was subsequently raised. Our final chance of the half fell to Neto, with a free-kick worked short to the Portuguese winger. He drove his shot to the near post, yet Kinsky got down to save and the game was goalless at the interval. The Blues have often made fast starts to second halves this season, but both sides nullified each other's threat in 15 minutes after the break. Much of the game was played in midfield, with attacks breaking down or being snuffed out. It wasn't until the hour mark that a shot was registered that threatened to break the deadlock. It came from Neto, who, after winning the ball and finding Palmer, reacted quickest to a rebound inside the area and drove a shot at Kinsky. The Tottenham stopper beat it behind for a corner. Our first change of the afternoon came soon after, with Marco Palestra coming on for Hato. The Italian dropped into a role on the left of our defence. Estevao's introduction followed; he replaced Quenda. Before the Brazilian's introduction came the game's biggest flashpoint. After Caicedo launched a counter-attack and was fouled in the process by van de Ven, a run from Palmer was halted by Mateus Fernandes falling and grabbing the ball. Several players came together, and three yellow cards followed, one of which went to Palmer. From the restart, we fashioned an opportunity as Palmer and Henderson combined to get Estevao in on goal from a tight angle. He fired at goal but into the side netting. With 13 minutes to play, and somewhat against the run of play, Tottenham went ahead. A corner was delivered into the Chelsea penalty area and van Hecke put Penders under pressure. The ball struck the hand of the Blues goalkeeper and deflected into our net despite Maxence Lacroix's efforts. Our task got harder as, three minutes later, Palmer caught Conor Gallagher in midfield and referee Chris Kavanagh deemed it worthy of a second yellow card, and a red followed. The game was effectively killed late on as a run and finish from Tel gave Tottenham a two-goal advantage in the closing stages, which they were able to see out to claim victory. The Blues are back in action on Wednesday evening as we take on Liverpool in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup. news.title: Alonso explains Joao Pedro absence plus Penders and Quenda selections against Tottenham
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has explained why Joao Pedro is not in the Chelsea squad for this afternoon’s game against Tottenham Hotspur – and emphasised the qualities Mike Penders and Geovany Quenda will bring on their full Premier League debuts. We are back at Stamford Bridge this afternoon for what the Blues manager expects to be an ‘intense game’ against our London rivals, whom we are aiming to defeat for an unprecedented seventh success in the Premier League. Alonso has made two changes to the team that started our win at Everton last weekend. One was expected as Penders replaces the injured Emi Martinez, who underwent jaw surgery after a nasty collision with Jarrad Branthwaite at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. The other is the absence of Joao Pedro, with Alonso explaining the Brazilian was ruled out of the contest yesterday. ‘He felt something yesterday in training,’ Alonso said. ‘At the moment, he has some fluid [around the injury], so we have to do some tests to see how big is the injury is. For sure, it’s a disappointment, but we need to carry on.’ Quenda is the man Alonso has opted to replace Joao Pedro with in the starting XI. It is the Portuguese winger’s first top-flight start in English football after his arrival in the summer. He has many qualities,’ Alonso said when asked about Quenda’s selection.’ He attacks the space well, is good with the ball, and is a threat. He’s been training well, and all the players will have their opportunities. Sometimes, they have to be more patient. Geo has been patient, and today it’s a big game to make his debut as a starter. 'We want to have mobility and to be fluid, so that we are not static and for sure with Geo we have those qualities.' Penders, meanwhile, starts in the Premier League for the first time, having made his debut off the bench against Everton last weekend. ‘I believe in every player we have and today it’s the first start in the PL for Mike,’ explained Alonso. ‘He showed last weekend against Everton that the can have a good impact. We need to deal with injuries and now he has a good chance, and we are fully confident.’ A big-game atmosphere is building at Stamford Bridge ahead of kick-off, and Alonso has highlighted the important role the Blues supporters play across the 90 minutes. 'It will be an intense game at a high tempo and high intensity on the pitch and in the stands. A proper derby. We expect an intense game with different moments for everything, with our qualities and the qualities of Tottenham. So it’s going to be very interesting.'

news.title: Under-18 Premier League report: Chelsea 4-1 Ipswich Town
news.body_en: Chelsea Under-18s came from behind to secure an impressive 4-1 victory over Ipswich Town at Cobham in the Under-18 Premier League, with Jacob Dako scoring a brace and Jacob Hall and Heze Grimwade always in target. After dominating the opening exchanges, the Blues fell behind in the 17th minute as Joel Ladegbaye swept home following an Ipswich counter-attack. We reacted positively, pushing for the leveller and probing the Ipswich back line on various occasions. Unfortunately, we couldn't apply a finishing touch before the break and went into the half-time interval a goal behind. The Blues continued to push in the second period, and our efforts paid off in the 66th minute as Dako found the net. That broke Ipswich's resistance and Hall netted soon after to put us ahead. We held that advantage until the closing stages – and then extended it as Ipswich attempted to salvage a point. Dako completed his double before Grimwade netted an excellent free-kick in stoppage time to seal a 4-1 victory. The Blues controlled the opening 15 minutes, although we were unable to consistently threaten the visitors' goal. Jashayde Greenwood did force a save from Ipswich goalkeeper Edward Twyman and Dako fired over the crossbar. After 17 minutes, we were punished on the counter, with Callum Stewart playing the final pass across the face of goal to enable Ladegbaye to sweep home and make it 1-0. We had a chance to level almost immediately, as Twyman raced out to clear his lines and missed the ball. Grimwade chased and lunged towards the ball, aiming to poke it into an empty net, but Pedro Felicio was there first to spare the goalkeeper’s blushes. We continued to search for an equaliser throughout the rest of the half. Ibrahim Rabbaj came close as he drifted inside and received the ball, but his left-footed attempt went just wide of the far post. We remained a persistent threat down the right, and Isaac McGillvary played a give-and-go with Rabbaj before cutting a pass to Greenwood. The Blues striker’s first-time shot was just off target. Towards the end of the half, Isaac Badu fashioned a great opportunity to level. The Portuguese youth international wriggled through midfield and played the ball to Greenwood, who lined up the shot before opting to tee up Rabbaj instead. But his shot was blocked and remained a goal down at the break. After the interval, it was more of the same, with the Blues holding onto the ball for long spells. Dako had two good chances in quick succession but was unable to convert either. Substitute Gabriel Sambou created the first, as he crossed into the penalty area for Dako, but he didn’t get enough on his header to steer it goalwards. Moments later, Greenwood drove towards goal and shimmied inside before laying the ball off to the midfielder, whose shot was dragged just wide. He was eventually rewarded with a goal, though. Captain Dante Waite played the ball behind the Tractor Boys’ defence, and Dako was able to tuck his finish into the net for his fifth league goal of the campaign. The Blues were a lot more like ourselves after Dako’s goal and, after Sambou had came agonisingly with a shot cleared off the line by Felicio. we scored our second just four minutes later. Hall gave us the advantage as he quickest when Twyman spilled a Dako free kick to place the ball into the corner. Having taken the lead, the Blues were oozing with confidence in the latter stages, and we began getting far more shots on target. Ipswich showed more attacking intent once they had fallen behind, but our defence handled the onslaught superbly. Dako then completed his brace to make it 3-1 with a neat finish into the bottom corner. The visitors' best chance fell to Kyle Messenger, who seemed set to halve the deficit. Toby Bell’s initial save was very impressive but the ball fell into Messenger’s path; fortunately, Hall made a fantastic recovery run and block. Grimwade got in on the action with the final kick of the game, scoring from a set piece once again. The 16-year-old wrapped the free-kick into the top left corner to end the game in style. This victory means we remain top of the table on 21 points, having won seven matches and scoring 37 goals. The Blues also extended our perfect run to five games. Chelsea Under-18s are back on the road next week when we face West Ham United on Saturday 31 October. The game gets underway at 11am BST and supporters can watch the match live with a CFC+ subscription. Alonso: We knew Lacroix's impact would be instant
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso believes Maxence Lacroix’s leadership and competitive nature have helped the centre-back quickly become an important member of his Chelsea team. Lacroix joined the Blues in the summer from fellow Londoners Crystal Palace after returning from the FIFA World Cup, where he was part of the France squad that reached the semi-finals. The defender has needed little time to adjust to his new surroundings across the capital and has become a central figure in Alonso’s plans, featuring in all our league fixtures so far this season – and starting all but one. A massive game is up next for the Blues, as Tottenham Hotspur visit Stamford Bridge this evening for a London derby that always gets the blood pumping in SW6. And ahead of that game, our manager discussed Lacroix’s strong start to life at Chelsea. Alonso said: ‘Max has many good things, but two of them are that he's ready – we knew that his impact was going to be instant with his Premier League experience, being competitive – and he has a strong personality. ‘He has great leadership. He likes to communicate, to be loud, to be very active in the game, and that presence is very important. ‘With the players around him, we are connecting better with him, and he's doing much better. He's doing good now, lately playing with Levi [Colwill] and when he has played with Wes [Fofana]. ‘We are very happy with him and he's feeling good.’ Don't miss your chance to experience the London derby in VIP style. news.title: From Where I Sit: The Harding family 💙
Alonso on harnessing passion and energy of ‘electric’ derby atmosphere
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso expects Chelsea supporters to create an 'electric' atmosphere inside Stamford Bridge during today's game against Tottenham Hotspur, which he believes will show the Premier League at its very best. Few occasions get Stamford Bridge bouncing quite like the visit of London rivals Tottenham to SW6; it's one of the first fixtures Blues supporters look out for when the Premier League fixtures are released each season. This match will be no different, with Alonso's side going into tomorrow's game in good form after back-to-back wins over Bournemouth and Everton. We are also looking for a club-record seventh consecutive home league victory over Spurs. Alonso is set to experience the atmosphere of a Chelsea versus Tottenham derby for the first time as Blues manager. But he knows what to expect and hopes the energy provided by the crowd can help his players to victory. ‘We are expecting a good atmosphere,’ he said. ‘Electric, with good energy, knowing that in a derby this passion is really in the air in the stadium. ‘We need to use it in a proper way because this is all about those games when you feel that excitement is something that you need. You don't need extra motivation; that will come naturally because of the history of the derby and because this is a top game. ‘We need that connection with the crowd in good moments. There will be tough moments, but we need to pull together and play our game. For me, it's fundamental that we play our game on the pitch. ‘The players, they do their best, but when the crowd is playing the game, is living it, that's the good thing about the Premier League. I think the crowd plays the game as well. It's not that they just watch the game. ‘They have great influence. When I say that spontaneously some energy is created in this league, it's because they feel that moment that: “Yes, I like what I see” and it's a big boost for the team.’ However, the Chelsea manager is aware that such emotionally charged atmospheres also require the players on the pitch to keep a level head to balance the passion with maturity, admitting that managing such situations in the Premier League is always a challenge mentally, but especially on occasions such as this. ‘It is very difficult,’ added Alonso. ‘That's why I've mentioned a few times that to find total dominance, a game when you are in full control and that you have no problems like in other leagues, it's difficult to find that in the Premier League unless you have become a top, top team. ‘That's why you can't rest when you are 2-0 up, because you know that if you concede one, the energy is coming, and you need to control that momentum. You can have mental preparation, but you need composure to deal with those moments. ‘I think that even in the Everton first half, we were 0-0, but there were a few [challenging] moments – 10 minutes of corner, throw-in, corner, throw-in. To go through those moments and to say, “Be calm guys, we know what we have to do, we have prepared for this and the other momentum will come”, for me it's fundamental.’ Don't miss your chance to experience the London derby in VIP style. news.title: Chelsea vs Tottenham: All you need to know
news.body_en: High-flying Chelsea return to the house of fun for a 5.30pm Saturday kick-off against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League at Stamford Bridge. Club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton look ahead to derby day in west London. Over the coming weekends Chelsea host successive league games against traditional foes before the next international break and they do not come weightier than this cross-city clash of west and north. It is the Blues’ first game this season in a time-slot that has not recently been fruitful, with just seven points taken from the last possible 21 and a current run of two straight losses. However, we are undefeated in the past eight London derbies home and away played at this time, including a 1-0 defeat of our capital rivals in the reverse fixture last season. Roberto De Zerbi’s visitors were winless in all top-flight games this season until beating Frank Lampard’s Coventry City 3-1 at home on Monday, climbing out of the relegation zone as a result. Xabi Alonso’s Blues made what felt like a step forward with Saturday’s 2-0 victory at bogey side Everton and returned to the UEFA Champions League qualification places. Chelsea have taken the lead in six of our seven league outings to date – the complete opposite to Spurs – and have taken an average of just four minutes to open the scoring at the Bridge. Last May, the corresponding fixture ended 2-1 with Enzo Fernandez and Andrey Santos netting for the hosts to extend Spurs’ relegation reckoning to the final day. Chelsea have a remarkable home record against our second-oldest top-flight capital rivals and can make club history by beating the Cockerels an unprecedented seventh time in a row in the Premier League. Up to now, the Blues have beaten the Lilywhites 83 times across all competitions, more than any other opponent. Alonso confirmed in his pre-match press conference after Friday's training session that Malo Gusto was fit to return against Tottenham, having missed our win at Everton the previous weekend, but Pep Chavarria, Jamie Gittens and Emiliano Martinez remain unavailable. 'Malo is fine,' the Blues manager explained. 'Pep is training a little bit more, but he is not going to make it [for the Tottenham game]. 'Emi had the surgery and day-by-day he is feeling better, but we still need to wait. A few weeks. Hopefully, less than more, but we need to wait.' Emmanuel Emegha will also miss out. The striker has yet to feature since arriving this summer, but is making progress in his comeback. ‘He’s feeling better, but we need to wait,' said Alonso. Chelsea are undefeated in eight league derbies with this kick-off time, since Boxing Day 2020, winning seven, including at Tottenham a year ago at the Bridge through Joao Pedro’s stealthy finish. Down the Thames at Craven Cottage in mid-January 2021, Mason Mount settled the result late on, and some time after Antonee Robinson had been red carded. Four months later in the return against Fulham at the Bridge, Kai Havertz struck twice without reply to claim all the points in the west London derby. The German also drew early first blood at Crystal Palace in April, with Christian Pulisic quickly making it two inside 10 minutes. Kurt Zouma added a third for the visitors before Christian Benteke pulled one back for the shell-shocked hosts. Pulisic’s second made the last quarter-hour comfortable and it finished 4-1 to Chelsea. Two weeks later, at West Ham United’s London Stadium, Timo Werner netted the only goal of the game in the first half, Fabian Balbuema’s 81st-minute dismissal easing any nerves. At Brentford in October 2021, with fans back in the stadium, Ben Chilwell was the only name on the scoresheet, on the brink of half-time, with our only shot on target as Edouard Mendy kept the Bees at bay for Thomas Tuchel. A year ago at the Bridge, against this weekend’s visitors, with early fireworks fizzing the night sky, Moises Caicedo pounced on defensive uncertainty to set up Joao Pedro for the 1-0 winner. At the end of January 2026, Jarrod Bowen curled in West Ham’s opener in west London and Crysencio Summerville doubled their shock lead before the break. But Nuno Espírito Santo’s side were taken to task in the second half, with Joao Pedro’s close-range header halving the deficit before Marc Cucurella’s brave dive produced the leveller. Joao Pedro turned provider for Fernandez to drive in what proved the decisive finish, after which Anthony Taylor resolved a stoppage-time fracas with a red card for visiting defender Jean-Clair Todibo. Tottenham are Morgan Rogers’ favourite opponent, the Chelsea forward scoring a career-high four times against the Lilywhites. The Blues have won 55.7 per cent of ground duels – the most in this season’s top flight. Chelsea have now scored three goals in the opening minute of a half in the Premier League to date, our joint-most in a single campaign (alongside the entire 2011/12 season). Until last Saturday at Everton, Chelsea had not kept a clean sheet in the Premier League since the same 2-0 scoreline at home to Brentford on 17 January, 22 games ago. Pedro Neto had never previously scored twice in a Premier League game, though he had netted a hat-trick for the Blues against Hull City in the FA Cup. news.title: Lacroix shares his journey from village life to the bright lights of the Bridge
news.body_en: Maxence Lacroix discusses his untypical footballing origins, in a farming village in the Dordogne region, and reveals his cultural hinterland in a wide-ranging interview for the matchday programme for Saturday’s Premier League game against Tottenham Hotspur. The France international defender grew up as one of a handful of kids playing football in the surrounding villages, where his parents both worked in the medical profession, and has risen to become a serial winner. 'It’s a farming village and there were maybe 300 people, with maybe five young children, because there were a lot of older people, or people who worked on the farms. My mother is a doctor, a general practitioner. And my father, he is working as a resuscitation nurse in the hospital. 'When I was young, I was quite close to wanting to be a vet, because animals were always close to me, you know. 'I started playing football at four. I was a goalkeeper, because my father was a goalkeeper. He put me on the field, because he loved football – he still does – and he said to me: "Okay, now it’s the time for you to start playing too".' The rest, as they say, is history, and now the 26-year-old is enjoying a year to remember, having gone to the FIFA World Cup off the back of a UEFA Conference League triumph with his former club Crystal Palace, then returned to London to begin the next chapter of his career with Chelsea. 'It’s going good,' he says of the season so far. 'I think we are in a better way, and you know, it was really quick for me, because I just left the national team, I had just a little bit of holidays and then I came back directly to playing the first game. So no, it was strange, but now I feel really settled in the team, so this is really good for me. 'It is fun, and it is a big team, you know – the players here are the best in the league. So I’m really happy to represent the badge and to be part of this big journey.' Elsewhere in the programme, club historian Rick Glanvill reflects on the impact Matthew Harding made on the club, as we mark the 30th anniversary of his tragic death in a helicopter crash on the way back from an away game at Bolton Wanderers in October 1996. The team that Harding’s investment helped to build went on to become one of the most cherished in Chelsea history, and their 6-1 win at White Hart Lane in December 1997 is the focus of our Greatest Games feature. Then there is all the info you need on the game ahead, plus the latest from around the club, including columns from Xabi Alonso and Reece James. So be sure to pick up your copy from the programme sellers around Stamford Bridge or order online from our publications partner, Reach Sport.

news.title: Update for fans attending match versus Tottenham
news.body_en: Ahead of Saturday’s match at Stamford Bridge, we have information to share regarding  Live Facial Recognition being used by the Metropolitan Police in the local area as well as expectations and measures regarding fan behaviour. The Metropolitan Police Service (MPS) has informed the club that on Saturday, Live Facial Recognition (LFR) will be deployed during the policing operation for the Chelsea versus Tottenham fixture.  The deployment follows the established stakeholder engagement approach previously used for football-related LFR deployments.  The two locations will be Earl's Court and West Brompton and two LFR vans will be deployed across these locations before the game. Signage will be deployed outside the zone of recognition in line with MPS LFR policy. The watchlist will contain individuals subject to Football Banning Orders relating to either club, together with persons wanted or missing for serious offences and those sought on warrants issued by HMCTS. The derby against Tottenham Hotspur is always one of our most anticipated games of the season and we are expecting nothing less than a passionate and vibrant atmosphere as we take on big London rivals. We welcome the part our supporters play in getting behind the team as the players target three wins in a row and victory in the first home London derby of the season.  We would like to remind supporters of their responsibilities in keeping support positive and ensuring that Stamford Bridge is a welcoming environment for all.   Discriminatory actions or language such as antisemitic or sectarian chanting have no place anywhere in football or society, and Chelsea is a club that actively celebrates our diversity. There are measures in place and strong sanctions against offenders to tackle discriminatory, anti-social and criminal behaviour. This could include suspension from attending all Chelsea matches, as well as potential police action. If you witness any anti-social or discriminatory behaviour on matchday, please report it to us.  Click below to use our reporting form for home matchdays.  This link will be active and the form available for use from three hours prior to kick-off until one hour after the final whistle.  - Click to access the reporting form At other times, click here to make a report. You can also report it in real time by using our reporting number. During the match text 88777 or 07894 93 77 93, with the stand, row, seat number and description of the offender and incident. All Premier League matches from 17 to 25 October are dedicated to No Room For Racism, reinforcing a collective commitment to tackling all forms of discrimination and promoting diversity within football. With Saturday being our home match during this period, a film will be shown inside Stamford Bridge, celebrating diversity as one of the game's greatest strengths. It will also highlight the impact racism can have on players, their families and communities, and encourages fans to challenge and report discriminatory behaviour. The No Room For Racism message will be displayed throughout the stadium, and players will be taking the knee to show solidarity against discrimination and send a clear message that racism has no place in our game or wider society. Supporters are reminded that engineering work affecting the District Line, with Fulham Broadway Station closed on Saturday, may have an impact on journeys to and from the match. Chelsea Football Club announces multi-year sleeve partnership with Sokin
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club can today announce a multi-year partnership with Sokin, the embedded finance and payments company used by businesses worldwide. Sokin will be named a Principal Partner and Official Business Payments and FX Partner of Chelsea FC and Chelsea FC Women. As a Principal Partner, Sokin will be represented on the sleeves of the Chelsea FC men’s, women’s and academy home, away, and third kits from the 2026/27 season. The partnership brings together two ambitious London-headquartered organisations with worldwide reach – a club with millions of fans across the world and a fintech platform through which businesses move more than $11 billion a year. A club of Chelsea’s scale works in many currencies every day, with partners, competitions and supporters around the world, and needs a financial partner built to handle that. Sokin gives finance teams business payments, multi-currency accounts, foreign exchange, checkout and treasury in one place, so they spend less time juggling banks and providers and keep more of what they move. As Official Business Payments and FX Partner, Sokin will simplify how Chelsea FC sends, receives and manages money in the currencies the club operates in. The Sokin logo will feature on the sleeve of the Chelsea shirt for the first time when the men’s team host Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on Saturday 24 October. Jason Gannon, President at Chelsea FC, said: 'At Chelsea, we seek to partner with organisations that share our ambition and innovative mindset. Sokin’s expertise in business payments, and their focus on making both simpler for the businesses they serve, makes them a natural fit for the Club. We are pleased to welcome Sokin to the Chelsea family and look forward to working together in the years ahead.' Vroon Modgill, CEO and founder at Sokin, said: 'Chelsea plays on the biggest stage in world football, and its business runs in dozens of currencies. Sokin was built for that with regulated, multi-currency payments and foreign exchange for organisations that operate internationally. 'We’re proud to be the platform behind the business payments and FX of one of the most iconic teams in football. Sokin’s platform serves businesses in more than 170 countries. We’re thrilled to be partners for the season ahead. An organisation as sophisticated as Chelsea doesn’t leave its finances to chance.'

news.title: Look who’s joined us on the sleeve 👀🔵
Alonso targeting a ‘complete’ performance to continue good run
news.body_en: Tottenham Hotspur's visit to Stamford Bridge tomorrow is the first of three high-profile fixtures in the space of the week for Xabi Alonso's side – and the Blues manager has stressed the qualities that must be shown to start with a positive result. We have lost to the side from north London just once in our past 41 meetings in SW6, but Alonso knows that record counts for nothing come kick-off on Saturday, when a new chapter in the rivalry will be written. With the Blues targeting a third straight league success for the first time since the start of this year, and Tottenham hoping to pick up a second victory this week, there is plenty on the line. Alonso knows what to expect. ‘We need to have a very complete game,’ he said. ‘Offensively, defensively, mentality-wise going through difficult moments, as there will be moments for everything. ‘We need to prove again we can continue our run, knowing it’s a special game. We need to play with our head, heart, with intelligence but with passionate energy. We will need many things tomorrow.’ On Tottenham, Alonso added: ‘I’ve seen a good team even in bad results, so we’re expecting a tough game against good opposition who do many good things. 'We need to be prepared for what to do in different moments with the ball. It’s going to be game eight [in the Premier League this season], so it’s still early days for everything.’ The meeting with Tottenham is the first of three high-profile fixtures in quick succession. Next week we travel to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup fourth round before hosting Manchester United. Alonso is excited for what is to come, and wants to see his side rise to the challenge and prove their credentials. ‘It was a matter of time until we had big games and this week we have three massive games against top clubs. This happens in the Premier League; this is not news. So we take it step by step, and we start tomorrow.’ Don't miss your chance to experience the London derby in VIP style. news.title: Ticketing update
news.body_en: As part of our commitment to provide transparency for our supporters across our ticketing policies and procedures, Chelsea FC is pleased to share an update on the progress of the newly introduced systems so far this season. The ticket application window was introduced for men's team matches for the 2026/27 season following supporter feedback regarding the ticketing process. After extensive fan consultation with multiple fan groups, the Fan Advisory Board and a supporter town hall, the ticket application window has been established to streamline the ticket purchase journey, make it fairer and more accessible for genuine Chelsea fans to purchase tickets, and reduce the risk of bot and tout activity. Similar systems are operated by a number of other Premier League clubs. We are pleased to share the results of the first six ticket application windows this season, to update supporters on how the process is working. Based on the data available for the ticket application windows this season, an eligible member applying for an individual match ticket via the ticket application window stood a 68% chance of securing a ticket. Overall, 99% of eligible members who applied for every Premier League game, have successfully secured at least one ticket, via the ticket application window, the ticket exchange or ticket forwarding, demonstrating the system provides greater opportunity for a larger number of fans to attend matches at Stamford Bridge. So far this season, of all fans who have applied in at least one ticket application window, 80% have secured a ticket for at least one match. The most in-demand fixtures are sold using a loyalty point threshold, to prioritise loyalty and regular match-going supporters. For the Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur fixtures, 46% of tickets were allocated to those who fell within the top 10% of total accumulated loyalty points. The ticket exchange and ticket forwarding function provides an additional route for supporters to access tickets. For those who were unsuccessful in the ticket application window, the ticket exchange represents a second chance of securing a ticket, with unsuccessful applicants having a minimum 48-hour priority window. We want to ensure genuine Chelsea fans are able to access tickets and we encourage all our supporters to use the ticket exchange and ticket forwarding to do so. For more information on using these mechanisms,  you can view our How-to Guides by clicking here. We also want to ensure that the next generation of Chelsea supporters have more opportunity to come to Stamford Bridge. So far this season, 76% of Junior Blue members who have applied in the ticket application window have been successful in securing at least one match ticket. The club continues to clamp down on ticket touting. In previous seasons, we have seen up to 80,000 bots per game attempt to access tickets online. Now, with the introduction of the ticket application window those using automated purchasing software are prevented from accessing on-sale windows and it enables increased monitoring of accounts to identify suspicious activity. We also continue to operate ticket collection points at home and away fixtures. So far this season, we have seen a 93% non-collection rate, demonstrating that our ongoing work to identify suspicious or fraudulent accounts is working. Using this data and supporter feedback, the club will continue to review our ticketing policies and processes, sharing regular insights with the Fan Advisory Board and updating Fans’ Forums.

Cobham Unseen: pre-Tottenham (h) 💪
Xabi Alonso says Mike Penders is ready to show his qualities
news.body_en: Mike Penders is expected to start his first Premier League game when Chelsea meet Tottenham tomorrow, and Xabi Alonso is confident the 21-year-old is prepared for the challenge that awaits. Penders was introduced midway through the second half of our victory at Everton last weekend, becoming our youngest Premier League goalkeeper. He replaced Emi Martinez, who took a heavy blow to the face and has subsequently undergone surgery on his jaw. With Martinez out for what Alonso says will be a ‘few weeks’, Penders is set to don the gloves for the Blues, with a mouthwatering London derby up first. ‘He is ready,’ said Alonso in his pre-match press conference. ‘He has been training well and played a couple of cup games where he showed he has a good level. Even the other day when he came on against Everton, he showed in a few minutes his personality and qualities. ‘This is why we have a squad, to be ready for these kinds of situations, and we are fully convinced that Mike can play very well. He is a goalkeeper for now and for the future. We are looking to the next games and are happy with Mike. He is prepared.’ Penders’ assimilation into English football has been aided in the past couple of months by Martinez, who brings a vast wealth of knowledge and know-how with him. Alonso explained how the Argentinean has helped Penders, who spent last season on loan at Strasbourg having signed for Chelsea in the summer of 2024. ‘He has the support and is learning from an experienced goalkeeper in Emi, who is having a great impact on the team and on Mike. ‘That happens in a very natural way. It’s not that we say, “Dibu, you have to be a mentor and you have this certificate.” It happens naturally, spontaneously every day because Emi likes to talk, not just with the other goalkeepers, but defenders as well. ‘He is very communicative and he likes to have this sense that they are close. So it’s happening.’ 'It has been noted that Penders bears similarities to former Chelsea goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, who Alonso worked with at Real Madrid. Our manager agrees there are resemblances between the two beyond simply their appearance and nationality. ‘The stature, both left-footed, both dominant in the air,’ Alonso pointed out. ‘I spoke with Thibaut when he was at the World Cup and asked about Mike, and he said himself that he could see the resemblance with Mike. 'We need to help him, support him, but for sure he is a goalkeeper for the present and the future.’ Don't miss your chance to experience the London derby in VIP style. news.title: Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea team news for Tottenham
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso confirmed Blues defender Malo Gusto is in contention to face Tottenham Hotspur tomorrow and provided updates on the fitness of Pep Chavarria, Emmanuel Emegha and Emi Martinez. The Blues welcome an old foe to Stamford Bridge tomorrow afternoon as Roberto De Zerbi brings his Spurs side to west London. We enter the game after impressive back-to-back top-flight victories: the first a 5-1 win over Bournemouth and the second a 2-0 triumph at Everton. Tottenham, meanwhile, recorded their first Premier League win of the campaign last time out. However, they are winless on the road this season. Alonso, who undertook his pre-match press conference duties after today's training session at Cobham, confirmed that Gusto was fit to return after missing our win on Merseyside last weekend. Chavarria, though, will remain absent. 'Malo is fine,' the Blues manager explained. 'Pep is training a little bit more, but he is not going to make it [for the Tottenham game]. Emegha will also miss out. The striker has yet to feature since arriving this summer, but is making progress in his comeback. ‘He’s feeling better, but we need to wait,' said Alonso. There will be no Martinez against Tottenham – or for a few weeks – due to the injury the Argentine sustained against Everton in a collision with Jarrad Branthwaite. Martinez was stretchered off in the second half and was taken to hospital for further checks, after which he underwent surgery on his jaw. Alonso confirmed the goalkeeper is doing well, but he will be sidelined for the matches ahead. 'Emi is doing better,' he said. 'He had the surgery and day by day he is feeling better, but we still need to wait. A few weeks. Hopefully, less than more, but we need to wait. 'The good thing is that he is feeling better and we need to listen to his feelings, the opinions of the doctors, the specialists, the surgeons. Considering it was a bad one, he is doing good.' news.title: Alonso Press Conference 🎙️
Lexi Potter on learnings from Keira Walsh and facing her former side
news.body_en: If there ever was an ideal role model for a young midfielder in the women’s game, it would be serial winner Keira Walsh. Our Chelsea Academy graduate Lexi Potter is now learning alongside her in the Blues first team, and she is thriving. It’s more than just master and apprentice, though. Potter’s calm head and confidence on the ball in the holding role has allowed Walsh to play higher up the pitch, to great success. When we sat down with the 20-year-old prodigy, she gave some insight into how the pair work together, and also into the general mood inside the camp at Chelsea. ‘Keira gives me a lot of confidence when I’m playing alongside her,’ Potter told us. ‘Especially when I'm receiving the ball out of possession. She gives me a lot of good information. We see the game in a similar way, and we're on the same page a lot of the time when we’re trying to progress the ball forward from a central area. ‘We’re in a really nice place as a team. For a while now, it's been really positive, and I think you can see it in the performances that everyone's working and fighting for each other.’ This Sunday, we face newly-promoted Crystal Palace away from home. Potter is best qualified to talk about the Eagles, having helped them earn promotion to the Women’s Super League in 2023/24. She immediately returned for a second season-long loan, gaining valuable experience in the WSL. Now, they are back in the top flight and the midfielder passes along some insight on what to expect from them. ‘I think it'll be a good game,’ she says. 'Having been at the club for two seasons, I know a few of the girls, and I’m looking forward to the game. ‘It was really special to be involved in their promotion. It was my first year in senior football, and I really enjoyed that season. I had a lot of opportunities, which I was grateful for. It was a really good season, and I  enjoyed it. ‘I was only 17, so I wasn't allowed to go for the full celebrations. But yeah, they were good; they were fun. It was a nice end to a good season. ‘The second season was a slightly different season to the first one. It was obviously a lot harder teams that we played. In terms of competition for places, it was a lot harder, and it was a different mindset. Potter added: ‘Getting minutes in the WSL at Palace really helped me because playing time is so valuable when you are developing. That exposure to the WSL really helped me during the loan. ‘When you’re a newly-promoted side, playing against the big teams was a really big challenge, and that’s always good for long-term development. I'm still in touch with a couple of the girls. I know Aimee (Everett), the captain, quite well and I speak to her fairly regularly. She really looked after me when I was there. ‘A few of the staff members there were really like impactful and really beneficial for me and my journey. I'm very lucky to have crossed paths with a lot of good people at the club. ‘They've had a good start to the season. They've picked up some really good results, so they'll put up a good challenge. They'll defend well, and we need to be on our game and try and break them down.’ Having now cemented her place in the Blues first team, our discussion concluded with our question about what she would say to any young players in the Chelsea Academy who are hoping to follow in her footsteps. ‘I'd say work hard and be patient,’ she concluded. ‘Your time will come. You just have to stay ready and work hard for it.’

news.title: Freddy Bernal signs new deal
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club is pleased to announce that Cobham Next Gen goalkeeper Freddy Bernal has signed a new contract, keeping him at the club until at least June 2029. Having joined Chelsea’s Academy as an Under-8, Bernal became a full-time scholar in 2025/26 and established himself for the Under-18s, winning the Under-18s Premier League title at Stamford Bridge. Bernal has since become a consistent presence between the sticks for Cobham Next Gen, making eight appearances so far and keeping a clean sheet in our latest EFL Trophy clash against Reading. The 18-year-old also gained valuable European experience last season in the UEFA Youth League, producing some standout performances against Bayern Munich, Benfica and Ajax. A reliable presence in goal, Bernal has demonstrated maturity throughout his progression at Chelsea. His form has also been recognised internationally with regular invitations to England youth camps. news.title: Morgan Rogers on bringing creativity, a ‘different’ front three and ageless Henderson
news.body_en: When Morgan Rogers gets the ball at his feet, there is only one thing on his mind. ‘The quickest way we can create a chance, whatever that may look like.’ That philosophy has served our No.17 superbly since his arrival at Stamford Bridge this summer. Rogers has had a telling impact in Xabi Alonso’s attack, providing four goals and four assists in his nine appearances to date. He has seamlessly adapted to life at Chelsea and has formed a potent partnership with Joao Pedro and his great mate Cole Palmer. Part of the reason it has been so successful is because of Rogers’ desire to make things happen. ‘I always want to be creative,’ he explains. ‘I always want to attack the goal and be threatening. Even if it doesn't work, even if it doesn't come off, I know I want the defenders thinking that I've got the ability to try something or something's going to happen here. ‘That's the way I've always been since I was younger. I think if someone is watching me, I'd want them to feel excited about watching the game and watching me play. ‘So I try and do everything I can in the little time or whatever time I've got on the ball, and just try and make as much of a difference as possible.’ Rogers has been aided by having his pal Palmer alongside him, as well as a striker at the top of his game in Joao Pedro. Between the three, 13 goals and ten assists have already been registered. That is some return just nine games into the campaign, and Rogers believes it is the variety of assets they bring that opponents have such difficulty dealing with. ‘A lot of it is chemistry, and I think we attack and challenge defenders in completely different ways,’ says Rogers. ‘We all want the ball in different ways. We all want different things in the game, and if they try and stop one, then the other two are going to get their joy because we're all so different. ‘If you get people that are the same and want the same, once you cut that off, you're struggling. But because we all want different things, if you try to stop Cole, then it allows me and Joao more space. If you try to stop me and Joao, then Cole's going to be free as a bird to set his authority on the game. ‘It’s kind of a mismatch for other teams of what to stop and how to stop it. We know that if we're all on it and we're all in the positive mindset of helping each other, that we're all going to get joy from the game.’ It is not only our attacking players that have caught the eye so far in 2026/27. Alonso has highlighted the importance of the collective in helping us become more robust defensively, and the addition of Jordan Henderson to our midfield in recent weeks has proven beneficial in that respect. Henderson, an England team-mate of Rogers’, covered more distance than anyone else on the pitch in our impressive recent victories over Bournemouth and Everton. His performances in a Chelsea shirt have come as no surprise to Rogers. ‘He's a special person, and a special player. People forget the player and just remember the person. They think he's here for experience and to help everyone, but people forget the player and what he's achieved in the game. ‘He can still play at the highest level. He can still outrun everyone. He’s so driven and he’s in such good shape. Thirty-six doesn’t mean anything to him, because he can still compete with 23- and 24-year-olds as he shows in training every day. ‘There’s no surprise to me that he can still impact games and impact teams because of his mentality, the way he thinks about the game, and the way he thinks about his body. 'Even if he's not at the training ground, he's thinking constantly about how he can be in the best physical and mental shape come the weekend to perform and deliver. ‘The more people talk about his age, the more fire it gives him to prove people wrong. So people need to keep calling him old and saying he's finished, because then he'll just keep getting better!’

news.body_en: The highlight of a fantastic 4-0 win over Manchester United exactly a decade ago was N'Golo Kante's first Chelsea goal. news.title: Key talking points from Sonia Bompastor's pre-Crystal Palace press conference
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor faced the media at Cobham ahead of our Women's Super League clash against Crystal Palace on Sunday, and here are the key talking points from what the Blues head coach said. For the fourth game in a row in the Women’s Super League, this Sunday brings a London derby for the Blues, as we travel away to Crystal Palace on a run of five consecutive wins in that competition. Bompastor confirmed that with the exception of Naomi Girma – who is recovering from a calf injury – every member of the squad is in contention to be involved against the Eagles, including potential debutant and Ballon d’Or nominee Manaka Matsukubo. Here are the rest of the key talking points from our head coach’s pre-match press conference on Thursday. ‘I think we need to carry over the confidence. Right now we are a team who is playing with confidence on the pitch. ‘On the defensive aspects probably on Sunday we didn't have time enough to remind everyone in terms of the game model what we wanted to achieve in all of the aspects of the defensive phase. It was a quick turnaround with the Tottenham game, but we had a good review with the players. ‘I think in possession of the ball we are carrying the fact we are creating a lot of opportunities in every game we are playing right now and we are being clinical and ruthless in the box as well. ‘So we need to carry over those positives going to the Sunday game.’ 'Giulia is a young, talented player. She joined us in the summer. I think for now you didn't have the opportunity to see her a lot with us. It means, again, right now I have a lot of players available and the competition is high in the squad. 'I'm really happy with Giulia joining us. I think sometimes for young players it takes a little while to settle in the team and to be able to get those minutes and to become a more important player for us, but I'm really pleased with Giulia's mentality. 'I think on and off the pitch she's a great person, great player. When she is on the pitch she works really hard. I'm really pleased with her mindset and mentality. She always wants to work hard, she always wants to improve, she's always keen to do more and I think, joining us, she's in a good place right now. 'I'm hoping for her to be able to get some minutes, some exposure. She played some minutes, but probably not at the level she would like to. But I'm confident because she has the right mindset and she's working with the right mentality. 'So I know these opportunities will come. I know she will be ready to take the opportunities and to show what she's capable of, and the quality she has as a player as well.' ‘Ellie is performing at a really good level. She's got two goals from her left foot, which is unusual. So right now she's performing at a really good level, being able to impact the game the way we want to play as a team. ‘She's really important out of possession and in possession, being able to repeat the efforts in that corridor. I think she brings a lot in possession of the ball, she always has this mindset and mentality to go forward. ‘She has a lot of pace, she's improving a lot in terms of the technical aspects. She's now able to deliver really good crosses, but also to be in the box and to be clinical to score some goals. ‘I'm not sure she can have a bigger impact than what she's doing right now, so it's great for us.’ ‘I think the key on those aspects is to have a regular conversation with Lauren. As you can see, when she's fit and available, she's one of the best in the world. ‘For us it's really important to get some feedback on how she feels because I think she knows her body, but also for us with the competence we have in the staff to make sure we make together the right plan for her. ‘It's making sure in terms of the load going into the game, she gets the right thing, because also we are in a team where all the aspects of the game plan and the game model are really demanding, with the ball, without the ball. ‘So we just make sure we do what is appropriate for her body, and it's a lot of conversations. We almost have a conversation with her every day and that's really important for us to get the plan right.' ‘I think it was really important. I think in every player’s journey it is important sometimes to go on loan and to play minutes in a different environment. Things are really different sometimes when you are in a different club, in a different environment. ‘Sometimes when you can be a player who is a leader but maybe not the main leader in a squad like the Chelsea squad, you can suddenly become the main leader in a different team. So I think for her, being a main leader in that environment was crucial. ‘The fact she could play many minutes for them was also crucial for her development, but also for her confidence. Coming back to us, it was also making sure we were giving her the opportunity to get these minutes and now to be in a place where she can perform on a consistent basis. ‘Now she just has the opportunity to play in most of the games, performing really well, and I think having that loan at Crystal Palace was probably really beneficial for her to be where she is right now.’

news.title: Bompastor Press Conference 🎙️
Sonia Bompastor delivers Chelsea team news ahead of Crystal Palace
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor provided the latest on Naomi Girma’s absence and hinted at a potential Chelsea Women debut for Manaka Matsukubo, as well as further involvement for returning captain Erin Cuthbert. The Blues face a yet another London derby in the Women’s Super League on Sunday, this time against newly promoted Crystal Palace. We are on a run of five consecutive wins in that competition, the last three of which have all been against sides from the capital – Tottenham Hotspur, West Ham United and Arsenal. Girma and summer signing Matsukubo both missed those victories due to injury and there was mixed news when Bompastor gave an update on their chances of featuring this weekend in her pre-match press conference on Thursday. ‘I didn't have much information on Naomi before,’ said our head coach. ‘I gave the earlier information before the international break, but actually Naomi is now dealing with a calf injury. ‘I think it will take a few weeks for her to get back, so for now she's just rehabbing. She's in a good place rehabbing and doing the things she has to do and to focus on. ‘We'll see, but I don't have any timeframe for now. I think otherwise I have the full squad available for the game on Sunday. ‘We had a few players who were involved in the Under-18 game and Manaka is also a player who could be in contention for the game on Sunday.’ One player who has already returned to action is Blues skipper Cuthbert, who came off the bench in the 6-2 win over Spurs at Stamford Bridge to make her first appearance since officially inheriting the captain’s armband for this season. For Bompastor, it seems the Scottish midfielder’s importance to the team cannot be overstated. ‘Erin is our captain, she's important on and off the pitch,’ Sonia explained. ‘I think she brings a lot of energy. I think the quality she has as a player in and out of possession, it's good news she's back with us. ‘In this block we will have to build her up to be able to start a game and to perform for 90 minutes, but we are having a lot of conversations with her. I think getting back to the team, playing 30 minutes in this league, is already a good step. ‘We have a plan for her all through this next block, we'll see what happens, but she's performing at a good level and in training this morning she was again good. I think she will help the team to get good results and to perform.’
